title: Textile workers protest in Surat demanding 8-hour shifts

tea.why: Textile and embroidery workers are protesting to demand proper implementation of labour laws, including an 8-hour workday and weekly paid leaves.
tea.want: Implementation of an 8-hour workday, a weekly paid holiday, and strict adherence to labour laws.
tea.changed: Oct 10: Around 20,000 unit owners gathered in Saniya Hemad to display unity and state they want labour codes implemented in toto.

summary: Textile and embroidery workers in Surat have been conducting a multi-day agitation demanding an 8-hour workday, a paid weekly holiday, and proper enforcement of labour laws. According to unions, many employees are forced to work 12-hour shifts despite legal protections. The protests began at embroidery units in Amroli and spread to other industrial areas. Industry representatives argue that fulfilling these demands entirely would raise production costs, though the Labour Department has held multiple rounds of meetings with unions and associations. Tensions during the agitation led to police registering three FIRs and arresting eight individuals following allegations of stone-pelting and forced factory closures. Meanwhile, unit owners gathered in Saniya Hemad to assert that they are willing to implement the new labour codes if adopted in full rather than selectively.
organizers: Textile Embroidery Jobwork Association of Surat
response: The Labour Department held several rounds of meetings with worker unions and industry representatives. Surat's Deputy Labour Commissioner directed industry associations to comply with labour laws. Police registered three FIRs and arrested eight people following allegations of stone-pelting and forced closures.
